statement: The function returns a result r, and r is the minimum value of |max(nums1) - min(nums2)| over all partitions of nums into two nonempty arrays nums1 and nums2, where a partition means every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums) is assigned to exactly one of nums1 or nums2, and nums1 and nums2 contain no other elements (their order is irrelevant).
preconditions: 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r (and does not fail by overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic) for every nums satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r.
preconditions: 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= (max_{0 <= i < len(nums)} nums[i]) - (min_{0 <= i < len(nums)} nums[i]).
preconditions: 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a partition of nums into two nonempty arrays nums1 and nums2 such that r = |max(nums1) - min(nums2)|.
preconditions: 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = min{ |nums[i] - nums[j]| : 0 <= i < j < len(nums) }.
preconditions: 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exist indices i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(nums) such that r = |nums[i] - nums[j]|.
preconditions: 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if there exist indices i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(nums) and nums[i] = nums[j].
preconditions: 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns results r for nums and r' for nums', r' = r.
preconditions: nums and nums' are slices with 2 <= len(nums) = len(nums') <= 100000 and all entries in [1, 1000000000]; nums' is a permutation of nums (same length and same multiset of entries).

statement: Whenever the function returns results r for nums and r' for nums', r' = c * r.
preconditions: nums is valid: 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and all entries lie in [1, 1000000000]; c is a positive integer and nums' is a slice with len(nums') = len(nums) and nums'[i] = c * nums[i] for all i, and nums' also satisfies 1 <= nums'[i] <= 1000000000 for all i.

statement: Whenever the function returns results r for nums and r' for nums', r' <= r.
preconditions: nums and nums' are slices with 2 <= len(nums) < len(nums') <= 100000 and all entries in [1, 1000000000]; the multiset of entries of nums is a sub-multiset of the multiset of entries of nums' with at least one extra element (equivalently, nums' can be obtained from nums by inserting one or more additional elements).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = min{ sorted[k+1] - sorted[k] : 0 <= k < len(nums)-1 }.
preconditions: nums is valid: 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and all entries lie in [1, 1000000000]; sorted is a nondecreasing rearrangement of nums, i.e. len(sorted) = len(nums), sorted[k] <= sorted[k+1] for 0 <= k < len(nums)-1, and sorted has the same multiset of entries as nums.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a partition of nums into two nonempty arrays nums1 and nums2 such that r = |max(nums1) - min(nums2)| and every element of nums1 is <= every element of nums2 (equivalently max(nums1) <= min(nums2)).
preconditions: 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every partition of nums into two nonempty arrays nums1 and nums2, r <= |max(nums1) - min(nums2)|.
preconditions: 2 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.
